documents.unit: University of Arkansas AI Task Force / AI working groups (ai.uark.edu)
documents.title: Guidelines for Acceptable Use of Artificial Intelligence
documents.stance_why: A coded delegates and B coded restrict. The guidelines say faculty 'are responsible for determining the appropriate uses of AI in their courses' and that the university 'encourages innovation and the use of AI', which supports delegates. But for coursework the document itself sets the rule: 'Student use of AI to satisfy course requirements or assessments is prohibited without the explicit permission of the course instructor'. That is the codebook's restrict (banned unless explicitly permitted) and matches the Libraries FAQ, which both coders coded restrict for the same rule. Instructors can lift the ban, but the default and the ban are the document's own, so restrict.
documents.summary: Campus-wide acceptable-use guidelines for AI covering ethics, integrity, teaching and learning, research, tool approval, data classification, privacy, reporting and enforcement. For coursework the default is that student AI use is prohibited without the instructor's explicit permission, and faculty decide what uses are appropriate. Most of the text addresses data security, approved tools and employee conduct.

units.why: The Purpose section ties the guidelines to state law: the university 'acknowledges its obligation stated in Arkansas legislative Act 848 of 2025 to address the authorized use of AI'. It frames the origin and scope of the document, so it is an institution-wide framework (P56).

units.policy: The university states it is obliged by Arkansas Act 848 of 2025 to address authorized use of AI.

units.why: The same sentence commits the university to 'facilitate the training of University students and employees' in AI. That is an institution-level training commitment, so P70 fits better than the framework type.

units.why: The text says 'accountability for all final decisions ... resides with human employees ... regardless of any AI recommendation', so AI cannot be the deciding party for institutional decisions. It is about decisions in the institution, not grading, so P73.
units.resolution_why: A coded informs/neutral, B must/restrict. The source says 'The University affirms that accountability for all final decisions ... resides with human employees ... regardless of any AI recommendation', which assigns responsibility to employees and limits AI as the decider, so must and restrict; actor stays admin because the university is the one affirming.

units.why: The university says it 'encourages innovation and the use of AI to enhance teaching, learning, research, and administrative functions'. This is a default welcome of AI use, P02.

units.why: AI use 'must be conducted in a manner that safeguards sensitive university data, protects individual privacy, and upholds ethical standards' states governing principles, so P56 rather than a specific data rule (P50).

The source sentence ('AI use must be conducted in a manner that safeguards sensitive university data, protects individual privacy, and upholds ethical standards') names data, privacy and ethics together as the condition on the encouragement just given, which is a principle for AI use as a whole, so P56 rather than the narrower personal-data type P50. Because it conditions the encouragement it restricts rather than permits.
units.anchor: AI use must be conducted in a manner that safeguards sensitive university data

units.why: The guidance 'supplements existing University of Arkansas policies' such as the Code of Computing Practices and must align with laws. This ties AI use to existing law and policy (P77).

units.why: The text warns AI 'could produce biased outputs relating to ... race, gender, ethnicity'. It names bias as a harm, so P53.

units.why: 'users should not passively accept its outputs without critical engagement' because AI may generate 'false content'. That is the verify-the-output rule, P31.

units.why: 'Students and University employees are ultimately responsible for the content that they produce, share, and submit' makes users own what they submit, matching P29.

units.anchor: AI must not be used to engage in any activity that is illegal, violates university

units.why: Citing Act 848, the text bars using AI to express a personal political opinion to an elected official or to lobby; this state-mandated employee rule matches no type, so UNCOVERED.
units.resolution_why: A coded one unit (P74, actor ta-staff) covering all four Act 848 items; B split them and coded the political-opinion item UNCOVERED. 'Express a personal political opinion to an elected official unless the opinion is within the scope of the employee's regular job duties or requested by an elected official or public entity' is a state-mandated limit on political speech, not a deceptive, fabricated or malicious use, so P74 would be a stretch and UNCOVERED is kept. The lobbying item (2) is a distinct rule and is coded as its own unit; item (3) repeats the illegal-activity ban already coded; item (4) is B's separate P74 unit. The sentence is addressed to AI use in general ('AI must not be used to'), so actor is all.
units.anchor: Express a personal political opinion to an elected official unless the opinion is
units.policy: AI must not be used to express a personal political opinion to an elected official unless the opinion is within the scope of the employee's regular job duties or requested by an elected official or public entity.

units.uncovered_note: Employees may not use AI to express personal political opinions to elected officials or to lobby, as required by Arkansas Act 848 (state-mandated limit on political speech). | Employees may not use AI to express personal political opinions to elected officials or to lobby, as required by Arkansas Act 848.

units.why: Item (2) of the Act 848 list, 'Engage in lobbying an elected official on a personal opinion if the employee is not a registered lobbyist for the public entity', is a separate ban from the political-opinion item; it matches no existing type, so UNCOVERED.
units.resolution_why: B coded the Act 848 items (1) and (2) together as one UNCOVERED unit and A coded all four as one P74 unit. Items (1) and (2) are distinct rules (expressing an opinion vs lobbying), so the lobbying ban is split out as its own unit; the Act 848 reference makes it a state-mandated limit on employees' AI use, which no type captures.
units.anchor: Engage in lobbying an elected official on a personal opinion
units.policy: AI must not be used to engage in lobbying an elected official on a personal opinion if the employee is not a registered lobbyist for the public entity.
units.uncovered_note: Employees may not use AI to lobby an elected official on a personal opinion unless registered lobbyists for the public entity, as required by Arkansas Act 848 (state-mandated limit on political activity).

units.why: The Act 848 list also bars AI use to 'override or avoid the security and system integrity procedures', a security-breaching use, P74.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. Item (4) of the Act 848 list, 'Intentionally override or avoid the security and system integrity procedures of the public entity', is a separate ban from items (1) and (2), so kept; A put all items into one unit.
units.anchor: Intentionally override or avoid the security and system integrity procedures of the public entity

units.why: 'Misrepresenting AI-generated work as one's own is prohibited' requires that submitted work be honestly the user's own; P29 fits because the rule bans misrepresentation, not generation itself (P19 would overstate it).

'The University's Research and Scholarly Misconduct Policy applies to work involving AI just as it does to any other work' says an existing policy covers AI, which is the P77 pattern (the same call as 'All existing IT conduct rules apply'); the policy is not triggered by a misuse event, so phase general. units.fit_note: Concerns research and scholarly misconduct specifically; P62 (govern AI use in research) is also close.

units.why: When AI helps make decisions with 'material impact on institutional operations (examples include admissions screening, hiring recommendations...)', 'the university will ensure that the use of AI is disclosed to appropriate stakeholders'. units.policy: For AI-assisted decisions with material impact on institutional operations, such as admissions screening, hiring recommendations or financial aid analysis, the university ensures AI use is disclosed to appropriate stakeholders and outcomes can be explained in understandable terms.
